notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order grouped by theme, not a chronology; surah order is not time order. Only six ayat speak of the Companions of the Ditch. The draft states them and nothing more; who they were is not stated in the Quran.

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, a wording that is also read as a curse on them.
The ayat speak of the fire full of fuel.
They were witnesses to what they did to the believers.
They resented the believers only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.
God is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is a witness over all things.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, and speaks of a fire full of fuel by which they sat [c1][c2][c3]. They resented the believers only because they believed in God, and God is a witness over all things [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, a wording that is also read as a curse on them [c1]. The ayat speak of the fire full of fuel [c2]. They were sitting by it [c3]. They were witnesses to what they did to the believers [c4]. They resented the believers only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy [c5]. God is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is a witness over all things [c6].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, a wording that is also read as a curse on them (85:4) [c1].
- The ayat speak of the fire full of fuel (85:5) [c2].
- They were sitting by it (85:6) [c3].
- They were witnesses to what they did to the believers (85:7) [c4].
- They resented the believers only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy (85:8) [c5].
- God is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is a witness over all things (85:9) [c6].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran tells of people who sat by a fire and watched what was done to the believers [c2][c3][c4]. They were angry with the believers only because the believers believed in God [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage names the believers' belief in God as the only thing the others resented, and ends by saying that God is a witness over all things [c5][c6]. One reading is that the ayat console those who are wronged for their belief [c5][c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the Companions of the Ditch were, where or when they lived, who the believers were, or how many; the Quran does not say.
- Not established: the ayat do not state that the believers were thrown into the fire; they speak of the fire and of what the Companions did to the believers.
- Not established: whether the ditch of the title and the fire are one thing; the ayat name the ditch only in 85:4.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the king, the place and the persons of the accounts later tradition tells about the Companions of the Ditch; none is used here.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about the Companions of the Ditch. None is used in this draft; a reviewer should note that the usual account comes from later reports and commentary, not from the ayat.
Wording a scholar should check first: 85:4 (slain or cursed), 85:7 (witnesses over what they did, or witnesses to it), 85:5 (the fire, as a fire of fuel).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the Companions of the Ditch and every detail of their story; none is used.
